events.summary: Speaker B suggested the macro facility may not be required now the remote is only for TV, so it may not be worth pursuing.

events.summary: Speaker C reported the research: open and specific questions asked of one hundred people about remote controls.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: we asked one hundred people their opinions on remote controls.

events.summary: Speaker C stated the survey covered one hundred people, split into small age groups of about ten to fifteen each.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: we asked one hundred people their opinions on remote controls.

events.summary: Speaker C reported that remotes are often lost and it takes minutes to find them.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: remotes are often lost. I often lose my remote control

events.summary: Speaker C reported that most buttons are not used, and that teletext is outdated.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: Most buttons are not used any more, like you said

events.summary: Speaker C reported that remote controls take too long to master and people hate using them.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: Takes too long to master the remote control.

events.summary: Speaker C reported that people aged fifteen to twenty five would be willing to pay extra for voice recognition software.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: most people would be willing to pay extra for voice recognition software.

events.summary: Speaker C reported that most people want remote controls to be pretty, fancy and different.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: most people want remote controls to be pretty, they want it to be fancy

events.summary: Speaker C proposed using existing open-source voice recognition software, so no research and development spend, but it needs microphones in the remote.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: voice recognition, the software, open source software exist already.

events.summary: Speaker C proposed dropping the regular button part so the remote can take any shape, such as a lollipop.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: imagine you got rid of the regular remote part

events.summary: Speaker C said about ninety eight percent of remote use is for changing channels.
events.speaker: C

events.quote: they say they do that about ninety eight percent of the time.

events.summary: Speaker C objected to voice-only control because it is impractical at night and when the remote is only trained for one person.

events.quote: voice recognition by itself, which I think is a bit impractical for like night time

events.summary: Speaker C questioned whether a voice recognition system is practical in a remote control.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: is it practical to have a voice recognition system in a remote control

events.summary: Speaker C objected that users may not wait through the training period and may be stuck with a bad remote for the first weeks.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: will people will people be willing to wait for the the period

events.summary: Speaker C objected that visitors and people with regional accents could not use a remote trained on one voice.
events.speaker: C

events.summary: Speaker C objected that users might return the remote because voice is not as fast as pressing a button.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: would they return it after a while because it's not as fast as pressing a button
